title: Jackson later held that epiphenomenal qualia could not be known, and became a physicalist

statements.text: Jackson changed his mind. In 1995 he argued that knowledge of qualia is impossible if qualia are epiphenomenal, so something must be wrong with the knowledge argument, and in 2003 and 2007 that it rests on a false view of sensory experience, answered by strong representationalism. He has abandoned property dualism for materialism.

sources.locator: section 5, 'The Dualist View About the Knowledge Argument'
sources.quote: Jackson (1995) argues that knowledge about qualia is impossible if qualia are epiphenomenal and he concludes that something must be wrong with the knowledge argument.
Jackson (2003) has abandoned property dualism in favour of materialism
